instructions: You are one of two independent readers for a public record that scores theories of consciousness. For the prediction below, answer two questions. (a) COULD IT FAIL: is there a result, stated or plainly implied in the wording, that would count against it, and that a study could actually observe? (b) DOES IT SEPARATE the theory from a rival: does at least one theory on the list of rivals predict something different (not merely stay silent)? If yes, name the rival or rivals, and say whether your view of the rival comes from the material given or from your own knowledge. Answer in JSON: {"could_fail": true|false, "separates": true|false, "separates_from": [ids], "rival_view_from": "material"|"own knowledge"|"both"|"none", "reason": "two to four plain sentences", "unsure": true|false, "unsure_why": "..."}.

core_claim.quote: A system has a point of view, in the plain sense that things happen to someone, when it separates the changes it causes from the changes the world causes and uses that difference.

source.citation: Fredrickson JA. Working Positions. Sentient Horizons, latest revision shown on the page 2026-10-24

prediction.statement: Cutting the copies of a system's own commands off from its senses, while the commands still work, leaves practised single actions running, makes the system lose track of which changes it caused, and also degrades its response to new events in the world, including ones that have nothing to do with it; and this loss differs from what losing feedback alone does.

first_stated.passage: Remove the split, meaning cut the copies of the system’s own commands off from its senses while leaving the commands themselves working, and the prediction is three things. Practised single actions carry on. The system loses track of which changes it caused. And, the part no one has yet tested, its response to new events in the world, including ones that have nothing to do with it, degrades too.

source.citation: Fredrickson JA. Working Positions. Sentient Horizons, latest revision shown on the page 2026-10-24

prediction.test_for: After the cut, response to new, unrelated events in the world degrades, in a way that differs from cutting off feedback alone, while practised single actions carry on.
prediction.test_against: After the cut, response to new events in the world carries on as before.

other_statements_of_the_prediction.passage: If the split can be removed in this precise way and response to new events in the world carries on as before, the split was not doing the work I think it does, and the bet loses.
